learning: Iteration 2 showed that a wider sensor span adds oscillation without fixing bends. If max_error on the s-bend and slalom stays near 0.06 with no progress gain, turn authority is the limit, so the next test is wheel_track 0.08 or a modest kp rise. If oval oscillation rises above about 0.3, the track is too narrow and kp or kd should move instead.
notes: Reverts the sensor array to the iteration 1 layout and narrows wheel_track to 0.09 m, following the Builder's proposal. Controller is iteration 1's with base_speed lowered to 1.7 to reduce bend overshoot.
rationale: Evidence: iteration 1 (score 337.6, best) used the 5-sensor array at ±0.03 m, y=0.07, wheel_track 0.10, kp 2.5, kd 0.4, base_speed 1.8. It finished 17 of 20 oval runs, with rms_error 0.021 and steering_oscillation 0.20. Iteration 2 widened the array to ±0.06 m with 7 sensors and kp 3.0. That cut oval finishes to 4 of 20, raised steering_oscillation to 0.37 and control_effort to 10.0, and gave no clear gain on the bends. So I keep the iteration 1 sensing and do not raise kp. Entity0 proposes reverting the array and narrowing wheel_track from 0.10 to 0.09 m. Narrowing raises turn rate per unit of turn by about 11% (0.10/0.09), which is the authority the bends lack. I keep kp at 2.5 so the extra authority does not add oscillation on the oval. I keep kd at 0.4 for damping. I lower base_speed from 1.8 to 1.7. On the bends the robot leaves the track at the 0.06 m limit, and iteration 2 at 1.7 raised s-bend progress from 0.236 to 0.316, although that change was confounded with the array. Oval mean finish at 1.8 was 1.73 s, so 1.7 should still leave room under 3 s. Expected result: max_error on s-bend and slalom falls toward 0.05 to 0.06, with oval oscillation staying near 0.2. This is a prediction and the next race will test it. line_loss stays last_direction, which recovered the tape edge in iteration 1.
